about_blocks.text: About Orca Lelum in Lantzville, BC

Orca Lelum is an Indigenous-led youth wellness centre at 699 Capilano Road in Lantzville, just north of Nanaimo on Vancouver Island. It serves Indigenous youth aged 12 to 18 who live in British Columbia and are dealing with substance use and mental health challenges. The centre says it is one of only two Indigenous youth wellness centres in the province, and its website currently shows that it is accepting intake applications.

about_blocks.text: The centre is run by the Orca Lelum Wellness Society. A Board of Directors representing nine Coast Salish member Nations governs it: Halalt, Lyackson, Malahat, Penelakut, Qualicum, Snaw-Naw-As, Snuneymuxw, Stz'uminus and Ts'uubaa-asatx. The centre sits on Snaw-Naw-As First Nation's ancestral lands, and it thanks the Nation for welcoming it there. More than 50 staff work at Orca Lelum, including regulated health professionals, counsellors, social workers, cultural coordinators, youth support workers, family wellness workers and aftercare workers.

about_blocks.text: Its main service is the Live-In Wellness Program, which has run since 2024. Youth live on site for 9 to 10 weeks. The program is voluntary and meant for youth with mild substance use and mental health challenges. Each young person has an individual care plan built with the Care Team, plus one-to-one counselling, group circles, equine therapy, trauma care, art and music therapy, tutoring and help with job readiness.

about_blocks.text: Culture leads the care here. The program is rooted in Snuw'uyulh (Coast Salish teachings) and the principle of Nutsamaat Shqwaluwun, working together with one heart and one mind. Youth take part in weaving, drumming, singing, storytelling and ceremonies such as blanket ceremonies, cedar brushings and spirit baths, with guidance from Elders and Knowledge Keepers. Days also include hiking, mountain biking, swimming, fishing and yoga.

about_blocks.text: Programming runs year-round, is co-ed and welcomes 2SLGBTQIA+ youth, and the building is wheelchair accessible. Youth need a valid BC Medical Services Card and a parent's or guardian's consent to attend. A withdrawal management program for 7 to 14 day stays is listed on the website as coming soon, at a new purpose-built centre, so detox is not offered yet. To start, email intake@orcalelum.ca or call 250-755-2144.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Orca Lelum

answer_blocks.text: Orca Lelum is for Indigenous youth aged 12 to 18 who live in British Columbia and have a valid BC Medical Services Card. Programming is co-ed and open to 2SLGBTQIA+ youth, and the facility is wheelchair accessible. Youth need parental or guardian consent, should be able to handle daily self-care and live with others, and are expected to take part in all parts of the program, including ceremony.

answer_blocks.text: Orca Lelum runs a voluntary Live-In Wellness Program where youth stay on site for 9 to 10 weeks. It is designed for youth with mild substance use and mental health challenges. The program combines Coast Salish cultural teachings and ceremony with clinical supports such as one-to-one counselling, group circles, equine therapy and trauma care.

faqs.question: How do I apply or make a referral?

answer_blocks.text: Email the Intake Team at intake@orcalelum.ca with your name and phone number, and say whether you are referring yourself or contacting them for someone else. Youth can fill in the intake package on their own or with a referring worker. A doctor or nurse practitioner must complete a pre-admission medical assessment.

faqs.question: How much does Orca Lelum cost?

answer_blocks.text: Orca Lelum does not publish a fee on its website. The BC government announced more than $7 million in provincial funding for the centre in April 2024, with another $1 million from Island Health, and it partners with the First Nations Health Authority. Ask the intake team about any costs, including travel.

faqs.question: Who might not be a fit for Orca Lelum?

answer_blocks.text: Orca Lelum cannot admit youth with unstable medical or psychiatric conditions, youth at imminent risk of suicide, or youth who need continuous one-to-one support or hospital-level care. Youth with psychiatric conditions, eating disorders, self-injury, aggressive behaviour, fire-setting or sex-related legal concerns are not ruled out, but the team will have extra conversations first to see whether it can meet their needs.

faqs.question: Where is Orca Lelum and how do I get there?

answer_blocks.text: Orca Lelum is at 699 Capilano Road in Lantzville, about 15 minutes north of Nanaimo on Vancouver Island. From Vancouver, plan on roughly 2.5 to 3 hours with the BC Ferries crossing from Horseshoe Bay to Departure Bay in Nanaimo. From Victoria it is about 1 hour 45 minutes north on Highway 1.

faqs.question: What happens after the live-in program?

answer_blocks.text: Before youth leave, they make a wellness plan and set goals for life after the program, and they learn tools to prevent relapse. The Orca Lelum team stays connected for up to 3 months afterward and helps with referrals to community resources. Family wellness work is part of the program too.
